# Qwen3.8-27B-CAN: a 27B model in 7 GB that runs usefully on a 4-core CPU

Unofficial derivative of [Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B) (Apache-2.0). It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Qwen or Alibaba.

**CAN** is an additive nibble code:
- Each group of 8 weights is the sum of 4 codewords, one from each of 4 codebooks of 16 entries.
- The weights are rotated by a block Hadamard transform (blocks of 512), with one fp16 scale per (row, 512 columns).
- Decoding is table lookups (`pshufb`), so the CPU kernel is fast.

The file was made in two stages: post-training quantization (PTQ), then a short knowledge distillation against the bf16 model that tunes only the scales and norms. The codes, codebooks and file size do not change.

## Files

| file | what | size | bits/weight (whole file) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`Qwen3.8-27B-CAN-kd.gguf`** | **recommended**: PTQ + KD | 7.0 GB | 2.046 |
| `Qwen3.8-27B-CAN.gguf` | PTQ only | 7.0 GB | 2.046 |
| `can3.patch` | llama.cpp patch with the CAN types (CPU only) | | |
| `ptq/`, `ptq_mtp/`, `kd/delta.npz` | the codes and the KD scales, to rebuild the GGUF | | |
| `resultados/` | logs, pre-registration and full report (in Portuguese) | | |

## Results

| model | bits/weight | GSM8K (N=1319) | share of bf16 | CPU generation tg128 (t/s) | CPU prompt pp512 (t/s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 original | 16 | 0.889 | 100 % | — | — |
| **CAN + KD (this repo)** | **2.05** | **0.876** | **98.6 %** | **5.75*** | **9.84*** |
| CAN, PTQ only | 2.05 | 0.825 | 92.8 % | 5.75 | 9.84 |
| our earlier ECTV/IQ2 file, with KD ([FardoX/Qwen3.8-27B-rapido-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/FardoX/Qwen3.8-27B-rapido-GGUF)) | 1.99 | 0.870 | 97.9 % | 2.57 | 8.28 |
| Q4_0 (`--pure`) | 4.51 | — | — | 3.25 | 5.87 |

- **CPU:** 4 vCPU (AMD EPYC 9655), binaries built for AVX2 only, `llama-bench -t 4`. Each figure is the median of 3 VMs. Generation is 1.77× Q4_0 (range 1.63–1.80) and 2.26× the ECTV file.
- **\*KD file speed:** speed was measured on the PTQ file. The KD file uses the same tensor types and kernels (only scale values differ), so the speed should be the same. We did not re-measure it.
- **GSM8K:** same harness for all rows, greedy decoding, max 768 tokens. The CAN rows ran on an exact F16 emulation of the CAN weights on GPU (A100). The bf16 and ECTV rows ran on an H100 on 22/11.
  - Integrity check on CPU: the real CAN kernels give WikiText-2 PPL 7.847, against 7.881 for the emulation (0.4 % apart).
- **Calibration and KD data:** C4 train plus text generated by the bf16 model. No GSM8K test and no WikiText data were used in calibration or KD.

## Honest caveats

- **One run per configuration**, with no repeated seeds. The GSM8K 95 % CI is about ±1.8 points.
- **The bf16 and CAN GSM8K numbers come from different GPUs** (H100 vs A100). Greedy decoding is close to deterministic, but not exactly across hardware.
- **Speed on other CPUs will differ.** On a larger AVX-512 server in a related test (Llama-2-7B), CAN's generation lead shrank to about 1.9×, and its prompt speed was below IQ2.
- **Text only.** We did not test vision. The MTP layer is in `ptq_mtp/` but is not used by the GGUF.

## Run (CPU)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp && cd llama.cpp
git checkout ad9d9e8f50e6ff9a6bfbbdd3aef6d74a8428cf4e && git apply ../can3.patch
cmake -B build -DGGML_CUDA=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=ON -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF && cmake --build build -j --target llama-cli llama-server
./build/bin/llama-server -m ../Qwen3.8-27B-CAN-kd.gguf -c 8192 -ngl 0
```

Stock llama.cpp cannot load these files. There are only CPU kernels (x86 AVX2): no CUDA, no Metal, no ARM.
